'''Buppou Shoryuji''' (仏法紹隆寺, Buppou Shoryuji) is a [[Buddhist temple|Zen Buddhist temple]] of the [[Kōyasan Shingon-shū|Koyasan Shingon Buddhism]] located in [[Suwa, Nagano|Suwa City]], [[Nagano Prefecture]]. Its [[Mountain name|sangō]] is [[Washizawa Sōgon-san]], and its [[Sect name]] is [[Daikokuzō-in]]. It is commonly known as Buppou-ji or [[Jigan-ji]].
[[File:仏法紹隆寺大イチョウ.jpg|thumb|180x180px|Buppou Shoryuji's large ginkgo tree. There is a tradition that considers the male ginkgo tree at Buppou Shoryuji and the female ginkgo tree on the premises of the Suwa Taisha Upper Shrine in Suwa City's Nakasu district as "husband and wife".]]
== History ==
According to temple tradition, in Daidō 1 (806), [[Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakaue Tamuramaro]], serving as a court lady to the [[Kamakura shogunate|Kamakura Shogunate]], established Buppou Shoryuji along with [[Jingū-ji|Shinjūji]] (which was abolished during the [[Haibutsu kishaku]]). It was named [[Jigan-ji]] as a branch temple (別当寺) of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Upper Shrine.
During the [[Kōnin (era)|Kōnin era]], under the guidance of [[Kūkai]] (also known as Kōbō Daishi), [[Jingū-ji|Shinjūji]] became a temple spreading the [[Shingon Buddhism]] and [[Jigan-ji]] served as a school for Shingon Buddhism, designated as a [[Jōhō Tanrinsho]], and hailed as "the foremost of the four temple schools in Shinshu". In Bunwa 1 (1352), under Master [[Shun-Kai Hōshi]], the temple site was relocated, and in Eiroku 3 (1560), during Master [[Sonzō Hōshi]]'s tenure, it moved to its current location and was renamed "Buppou Shoryuji". During the Edo period, it became a prayer temple for the [[Suwa Takashima Domain]]. In the Taishō period, it encountered a great fire, destroying the main hall, kitchen, founding hall, Kongōden, and corridors, but the main hall, kitchen, and founding hall were rebuilt. In Heisei 1 (1989), [[Chieidō]] was established.
[[File:諏訪大明神御本地普賢菩薩像 - Suwa Daimyōjin as Bodhisattva Samantabhadra (Fugen Bosatsu).jpg|thumb|Chieidō of Buppou Shoryuji. It is believed that the large ginkgo tree on the grounds of the Suwa Taisha Upper Shrine in Suwa City's Nakasu district and the male ginkgo tree at Buppou Shoryuji are "husband and wife" trees.]]
== Overview ==
The main deities enshrined are the esoteric Buddha [[Vairocana|Dainichi Nyorai]] and [[Bhaisajyaguru|Yakushi Nyorai]].
According to Genso no Kōsei-in's "Shinshu Shimuki" of [[Daigo-ji Risei-in]] in Kyoto, in Tenbun 2 (1533), during the transmission and consecration (灌頂) of doctrines and bonds at [[Bun'ei-ji]] in [[Iida, Nagano|Iida City]], it is recorded that "the ritual implements were brought from Suwa's Buppou Shoryuji." This indicates that Buppou Shoryuji is a venerable ancient temple that houses significant ritual implements, documents, and sutras from the Heian to Sengoku periods. Climbing up from the old [[Kōshū Kaidō]], there is a mountain gate that used to be the main gate of [[Jingū-ji|Shinjūji]], and within the temple grounds is a large ginkgo tree (a cultural property of Suwa City, estimated age over 500 years). In front of the main hall, there is [[Seitendo]], [[Fudōdō]] on the left side, and the kitchen on the right side. Behind the main hall's [[Ikezen Shūyō-shiki Teien]] is the [[Fugen-dō]], which was relocated in 1975 from [[Koyasan Tokyo Betsuin]]. This building is a [[Tented roof|Hōkei-zukuri]] structure built in Enpō 1 (1673), featuring a pseudo-jewel enshrouded corridor with a one-room worship hall attached. Inside the hall, the main deity of Shinjūji's [[Fugen-dō]], [[Samantabhadra (Bodhisattva)|Fugen Bosatsu]] (a cultural property of Suwa City), is enshrined as the [[Honji suijaku|Honchi-butsu]] donated by [[Chikuatsu Atsuyuki]] in En'ei 1 (1293) as the [[Honji suijaku|Honchi-butsu]] of [[Suwa Daimyōjin]]. Additionally, the [[Fugen Bosatsu Riding Elephant Statue]] (a [[Nagano Prefecture Cultural Property]]) from Shinjūji's [[Nyo-hōin]] [[Fugen Bosatsu Riding Elephant Statue]] has also been relocated here.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://archive.md/pByUp |title=...|qq=}}</ref>
During the [[Meiji era]] 15 year (1882), the Seiryōdō built that year enshrined a separate deity of the Rinzai School from [[Daigo-ji Risei-in]].
Additionally, the temple houses cultural properties including 600 scrolls of the ancient [[Sutra of the Great Prajñāpāramitā]], 13 ancient sutras from the Eiroku period onward, an image of [[Acala|Fudō Myōō]] from the Kamakura period (a [[Nagano Prefecture Cultural Property]]), and paintings of the [[Juroku Zenjin]].
== Access ==
* From [[Chūō Main Line|JR Chūō Line]] [[Kami-Suwa Station]] via [[Suwa Bus]] "Shiga Branch Office Front" stop, approximately 10 minutes on foot.
